name: Corey's Calabrian Chili
description: A spicy Korean-Italian fusion vegetarian chili with complex heat from gochujang and Calabrian chilis

equipment.item: Dutch oven or large heavy-bottomed pot
equipment.notes: Needs to hold at least 6 quarts
At least 3 medium and 2 small bowls

equipment.alternative: Dedicate a counter area for staging

ingredients.notes: Adds richness and helps bloom spices
For stirring in, plus more for garnish

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: clear a section of counter and place a half sheet pan there if you have one. Get out: 3 medium bowls (for vegetables), 2 small bowls (for spices and pastes), and your cutting board.
prep_steps.notes: Having everything organized prevents scrambling while the onions cook

prep_steps.instruction: Chop the red onion into 1/2-inch pieces and transfer to medium bowl #1
prep_steps.notes: This goes in first and cooks longest

prep_steps.instruction: Chop the red bell pepper into 1/2-inch pieces and add to medium bowl #1 with the onion
prep_steps.notes: Bell pepper goes in with onion later, so they can share a bowl

prep_steps.instruction: Chop the carrots into 1/4-inch half-moons and transfer to medium bowl #2
prep_steps.notes: Carrots go in at a different time than onion

prep_steps.instruction: Chop the celery into 1/4-inch slices and add to medium bowl #2 with the carrots
Press or mince the garlic and transfer to a small bowl
prep_steps.notes: Keep separate - garlic goes in with the pastes

prep_steps.instruction: Measure all dry spices into small bowl #1: cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, Aleppo pepper, cayenne, and black pepper
prep_steps.notes: These all bloom together in the butter

prep_steps.instruction: Measure gochujang, Calabrian chili paste, and chili oil into small bowl #2
prep_steps.notes: These add together after the garlic

prep_steps.instruction: Open and drain all 4 cans of beans in a strainer. Rinse well under cold water and let drain. Transfer to medium bowl #3.
prep_steps.notes: Rinsing removes excess sodium and starchy liquid

prep_steps.instruction: Open the can of diced tomatoes (do not drain). Keep in the can or transfer to a measuring cup.
Measure 3 cups water into a large measuring cup. Add the bouillon paste and stir to dissolve.
prep_steps.notes: Dissolving the paste first ensures even distribution

prep_steps.instruction: Chop cilantro and set aside in a small pile on the cutting board
prep_steps.notes: This goes in at the very end - doesn't need its own bowl

cook_steps.instruction: Melt butter in Dutch oven over medium heat

cues.visual: Butter is fully melted and beginning to foam
cues.audio: Gentle sizzle as water cooks off

cook_steps.instruction: Add chopped onion from medium bowl #1 (save the bell pepper in the bowl). Season with a pinch of salt. Sweat until translucent.

cues.visual: Onion is soft, translucent, not browned

cook_steps.warnings: If onions start to brown, reduce heat - we want to sweat, not sauté

cook_steps.instruction: Add the spice blend from small bowl #1 directly to the onions. Stir constantly to bloom the spices.

cues.visual: Spices coat the onions evenly, mixture darkens slightly
cues.aroma: Toasty, warm, complex spice aroma - this is the moment the dish comes alive

cook_steps.warnings: Stir constantly - spices burn quickly. Reduce heat if smoking.

cook_steps.instruction: Add carrots and celery from medium bowl #2. Add bell pepper from medium bowl #1. Season with salt. Cook until carrots begin to soften.

cues.visual: Carrots lose their raw, pale look, edges start to soften
cues.aroma: Sweet vegetable smell joins the spices

cook_steps.instruction: Add minced garlic from the small bowl. Add the paste mixture (gochujang, Calabrian chili, chili oil) from small bowl #2. Stir to combine and cook briefly.

cues.visual: Pastes coat everything in a red-orange glaze

cook_steps.warnings: Don't let garlic burn - keep stirring

cook_steps.instruction: Add diced tomatoes with all their juices. Add drained beans from medium bowl #3. Pour in the bouillon water. Add bay leaf. Stir well to combine everything.

cues.visual: Everything is submerged in liquid, mixture looks hearty

cook_steps.instruction: Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally.

cues.visual: Liquid has reduced and thickened, beans are starting to break down at edges

cook_steps.warnings: Stir every 5-10 minutes to prevent sticking on bottom

cook_steps.instruction: For thicker consistency: use immersion blender to pulse 5-6 times directly in pot. OR transfer 1 1/2 cups to regular blender, blend smooth, return to pot.

cues.visual: Some beans broken down, chili has body but still has texture

cook_steps.warnings: If using regular blender, vent the lid and cover with towel - hot liquids can explode

cook_steps.instruction: Remove from heat. Remove and discard bay leaf. Stir in chopped cilantro from cutting board. Add sherry vinegar to taste. Taste and adjust salt.
cook_steps.warnings: Vinegar should brighten flavors without tasting sour

finishing.instructions: Ladle into bowls. Top with any or all: sliced avocado, sour cream, grated cheddar, fresh cilantro, tortilla chips, extra chili oil for more heat.
finishing.make_ahead: Chili keeps refrigerated for 5 days and improves overnight as flavors meld. Can be frozen for up to 3 months.
finishing.storage: Store in airtight container. Reheat gently on stovetop, adding splash of water if too thick.

notes: The butter is essential - it adds richness and helps bloom the spices better than oil
Be generous with the bouillon paste - it provides the savory backbone
The gochujang and Calabrian chili combo gives complex, layered heat that builds but doesn't overwhelm
Don't skip sweating the onions properly - this builds the flavor foundation
Adapted from Cookie and Kate's Vegetarian Chili with Korean-Italian fusion modifications
